status: QA guardrail for Lesson 1-14 enrichment; not a public content surface yet
purpose: Keep teacher-source facts separate from learner-aid enrichment, especially Hanja, Chinese glosses, and word-origin notes.

tiers.label: Teacher Source
tiers.definition: A fact, form, classroom contrast, example family, or pragmatic point grounded in the teacher PPTs or another named course source through sourceRefs.

tiers.label: Verified Enrichment
tiers.definition: A learner aid that goes beyond the teacher source and has been checked against an explicit dictionary, instructor review, or other named reference.

tiers.label: Unverified Enrichment
tiers.definition: Assistant-added learner support that is useful for review but has not yet been independently verified and should be hidden or visibly labeled before public display.

notes: All Lesson 1-14 packs now declare Hanja, Chinese glosses, originType, and originNote as unverified enrichment until a separate verification pass promotes them.
Teacher PPT sourceRefs still establish the classroom vocabulary/grammar surface, but they do not automatically verify Hanja, Mandarin gloss fit, or etymology.
The only obvious malformed Hanja field found in this pass was removed from v4-of, where the particle 의 had been placed in hanja.
The standalone Explore vocabulary enrichment file includes Hanja, Chinese, and originNote fields for learner support.
Do not treat this file as teacher-source content. Hanja and origin notes should be hidden or visibly labeled until reviewed.
No Hanja, Chinese gloss, or word-origin item has been promoted to verified-enrichment in this repository snapshot.

promotionChecklist: Record the reference used to verify the Hanja, Chinese gloss, or word-origin note.
Check Korean sense and Mandarin sense separately; shared characters do not guarantee matching modern usage.
Mark mixed/native/loanword items explicitly instead of forcing them into a Sino-Korean bucket.
Keep classroom sourceRefs separate from enrichment verification references.
